Hi Maya,

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement at GreenStack is ready to proceed but they need a completed 'preferred vendor' form and a sample PO with line-itemization that our accounting team can route. Our controller is uncomfortable with a purely variable per-token billing line unless there's a way to map it to a committed annual spend and SKU lines for the PO.

Specifically they asked: 1) Can you provide a vendor form (we attached ours) with Redwood's tax & payment info? 2) Can you show how the per-token pricing would appear as PO line items (SKU + description + unit price) for an annual commitment? 3) Do you accept invoices net-30 and can we receive monthly invoices against a single PO?

Can you confirm and attach the vendor form back with the suggested PO line items?

Appreciate it,

Hi Liam —

Thanks for the clear ask and for sending your vendor form. Short answers up front: yes, we can complete your vendor form; yes, we can accept net-30 invoices; and yes, we can structure PO line items that map to a committed annual spend while keeping the underlying billing usage-based.

Notes on approach (high level):
- We typically map per-token tiers into monthly/annual committed spend line items. For example, a 1M-token/month commitment at an agreed effective per-token rate can be represented as a monthly SKU (e.g., RW-HOST-API-COMMIT-M1) with unit = "monthly committed capacity" and unit price = $X. Actual monthly invoices then reconcile against realized usage, with credits or overage lines as needed.

- This keeps your accounting happy (fixed PO lines) while preserving Redwood's usage-based flexibility.

I'll loop in finance and legal with the vendor form and a sample PO mapping. Can you confirm the exact PO/accounting fields GreenStack requires on the form (e.g., remit-to address, W9, GL code placeholder)? If you want, attach a sample internal PO and I'll mirror the line-item formatting.

I'll send a filled vendor form and a CSV mapping with SKU examples by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Maya

Thanks Maya — reviewed the draft mapping. We can accept the PO layout GreenStack prefers, with the following operational notes:

- Invoice flow: We will issue monthly invoices net-30 against the single annual PO. Each invoice will include: (a) monthly committed SKU line (fixed amount for the committed capacity), (b) usage reconciliation line showing actual tokens consumed and effective per-token rate, and (c) overage or credit line if usage >/ < commitment.
- Minimum billing floor: Finance recommends a modest monthly minimum to avoid micro-billing administrative overhead. Proposal: a $1,000/month administrative floor for this agreement (waived if annual realized usage >= committed spend).
- GL code: we'll populate a placeholder and accept the customer's GL code field on the PO.
- W9 & tax: we'll attach our W9 and vendor profile to the vendor form.

I've attached a sample invoice and a completed W9. Legal please confirm any additional clauses — Soojin?

Rachel Kim

Hi Liam / GreenStack procurement —

Thanks for your patience. Attached are the completed items you requested:
- Vendor form: VendorForm_filled_by_Redwood.pdf (we populated legal name, EIN, remit-to, W9 included)
- Sample PO line-item mapping: Redwood_PRICING-MAPPING-2026Q4.csv (contains SKU codes we propose to reference on the PO: RW-HOST-COMMIT-M1, RW-HOST-COMMIT-M5, RW-HOST-COMMIT-ANNUAL etc.)
- Invoice example: Redwood_Invoice_Sample.pdf showing committed line, usage reconciliation, and overage/credit lines.

Summary of the billing proposal:
- PO structure: GreenStack issues a single annual PO that references monthly SKU lines (qty=12) or an annual SKU if you prefer one line. Example: RW-HOST-COMMIT-M1 — Description: "Hosted API committed capacity (1M tokens/month)" — Unit price = $2,400 — QTY=12 -> annual committed spend = $28,800.
- Overage handling: If monthly usage > committed tokens, we bill overage at the agreed per-token overage rate on the same invoice line set. If usage < committed, we apply credit against the committed line or carry forward credit per the PO's terms.
- Monthly minimum: Redwood proposes a $1,000/month administrative floor as discussed by Finance; happy to set this to $0 at a different tier if GreenStack prefers.
- Next steps: If this looks good I can return the vendor form signed and we can provide a DocuSign for a short SOW that references the PO and commit quantities. Attached is a DocuSign link for the SOW/committed schedule: https://www.docusign.com/link/abc123

Would you like us to switch the PO to an annual single-line SKU instead of 12 monthly lines? Happy to adapt to your AP process — let me know which format your system prefers so I can mirror it exactly.

Thanks,
Maya
